That nagging ache right at the front of your shoulder during bench or chin-ups? The biceps tendon is often involved.

It tends to flare with a jump in overhead or pressing work, heavy carrying, or alongside other shoulder niggles. Most people don't need to stop training. Easing back on the lifts that provoke it while keeping everything else going usually works better than full rest.

From there, gradual strengthening for the biceps, rotator cuff and shoulder blade muscles does the heavy lifting.

caption:
Copped a knee to the thigh at touch footy or cricket? Here's what tends to help in the first few days.

A corked thigh is a deep bruise in the muscle. In the first 48 hours, relative rest, ice, compression and elevation are common steps. Skip the HARM: heat, alcohol, running and massage on the area can increase bleeding in the muscle.

As pain allows, gentle knee bending, walking and light cycling help restore movement, then build towards jogging and sport in steps rather than testing it with a sprint.

Swelling that keeps increasing, a very tight or numb thigh, or being unable to bend the knee needs prompt medical assessment. Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can guide your return. Book online via the link in bio.

Rested that sore tendon for weeks, only for it to flare the moment you go back?

caption:
Legs fine on the way up, knees complaining on the way down? Descents are often the harder part.

Going downhill, your thigh muscles work as brakes while they lengthen, which loads the front of the knee more than climbing. Tired legs late in a hike make it harder still.

Shorter steps, a slight knee bend, zigzagging down steep sections and walking poles can all help share the load. At home, slow step-downs, split squats and wall sits can help build capacity over a few weeks.

The trick is starting slower than feels necessary. Try one minute of easy jogging and two minutes of walking, eight times over, three days a week. Add a little each week, and repeat any week that felt tough. Many beginners take around eight to ten weeks to get there.

Two short strength sessions a week help your legs cope. In summer, run early or late, carry water and slow down on hot days.

Momo's bridges kept landing in her lower back instead of her glutes. Your glutes help control your hips and knees every time you walk, run, climb stairs or lift.

Momo's hip clunks when she lifts her leg. In most cases that noise is harmless: if there's no pain and you move normally, it's often just a tendon sliding over bone.

It's a different story when the click comes with deep groin pain, catching, locking or a feeling the hip might give way. That combination is worth getting assessed. Strengthening the glutes, hip flexors and trunk, and adjusting the moves that provoke it, is often part of the plan.

caption:
A back flare-up doesn't have to mean giving up Pilates. It usually means changing how you do it for a little while.

Once the worst has settled and you can walk, sit and sleep reasonably, gentle movement often helps. Start with shorter sessions, lighter springs and smaller ranges, and use a simple rule: if your back feels the same or better within 24 hours, you're on track. Let your instructor know what happened.

Leg numbness or weakness, pain that keeps climbing, or bladder or bowel changes need medical attention first. At Hybrid Physio, our Pilates team works alongside our physios, so your program can change as your back does. Book online via the link in bio.
